title: The Soul Train Episode
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss Soul Train, the nationally syndicated music and dance TV show created and hosted by Don Cornelius. They cover its origins as Chicago house parties, the black-and-white local pilot funded by Cornelius, its move to Los Angeles and syndication, the Soul Train Line and dancers, sponsors Johnson Products (Afro Sheen and Ultra Sheen), notable performers, dancers who became stars (Jody Watley, Rosie Perez, Jermaine Stewart, Cheryl Song, Carmen Electra), Dick Clark's rival show Soul Unlimited, Cornelius's later years and death, and the show's long run to 2006. The episode closes with a listener mail about Iron Maiden.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and Soul Train's legacy
segments.summary: Hosts reminisce about watching Soul Train as kids and discuss how it presented Black culture on TV on its own terms, unlike earlier shows like American Bandstand.

segments.title: Dancers as trendsetters and cultural influence
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how Soul Train dancers set trends, that dance moves like the Robot and the Backslide debuted on the show, and quotes from Cornel West and Common about its importance.

segments.title: Soul Train versus American Bandstand and Dick Clark
segments.summary: A 1973 TV critic compared Soul Train unfavorably to American Bandstand, and the hosts discuss Dick Clark's reaction.

segments.title: Don Cornelius as owner and creator
segments.summary: Cornelius owned Soul Train outright, unusual for a show creator; the James Brown anecdote illustrates his ownership.

segments.title: Early life and career of Don Cornelius
segments.summary: Cornelius grew up on Chicago's South Side, served in the Marines, worked as a Chicago police officer, then left to train in broadcasting after a radio newsman praised his voice.

segments.title: Origins of Soul Train as Chicago house parties
segments.summary: Cornelius worked as a TV news reporter and DJ, hosted house parties he called the Soul Train, and funded a black-and-white pilot himself with four hundred dollars.

segments.title: Syndication, sponsors and Johnson Products
segments.summary: Soul Train moved to Los Angeles and was nationally syndicated while the Chicago local edition continued. Johnson Products' Afro Sheen and Ultra Sheen became key sponsors.

segments.title: Performers, WCIU anecdotes and the Soul Train Line
segments.summary: Early guests included Gladys Knight and the Pips on the first syndicated episode; the hosts describe the WCIU station, the show's format, and the Soul Train Line dancers.

segments.title: Dancers, Clinton Ghent and stars who came from the show
segments.summary: Dancers were scouted from clubs, unpaid, and filmed on weekends under Cornelius's rules. Clinton Ghent helped build a family atmosphere. Jody Watley, Jeffrey Daniel, Shalimar, Carmen Electra, Jermaine Stewart and Cheryl Song all came from the show.

segments.title: Rosie Perez incident and Cornelius's personal conduct
segments.summary: Rosie Perez's account of a contract dispute with Cornelius, and the hosts note he was later charged with domestic violence and intimidating a witness.

segments.title: Dick Clark's Soul Unlimited and Elton John
segments.summary: Dick Clark launched Soul Unlimited on ABC as a rival to Soul Train; it was canceled after a few episodes. Later performers included David Bowie and Elton John.

segments.title: Hip hop era, Public Enemy and later years
segments.summary: In the eighties Cornelius reportedly disliked hip hop, and his interview with Public Enemy is discussed. He stepped down in the early nineties; the show ran until 2006. Cornelius died by suicide amid illness, and his legacy is discussed.

segments.title: Listener mail about Iron Maiden
segments.summary: A listener from Western Australia writes about Iron Maiden and praises the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with the usual sign-off and contact information.
